messages.author: 6824c1e1fe15ab15
messages.subject: Ground Temperature
parts:
Is it possible to use the climate functions to calculate ground temperature at a given spot for a particular combination of air temperature x and solar radiation y? From what I can tell, the functions in the R package rely on external data gathered from other sources, so I can't manually input a combination of air temperature and solar radiation.

If not, is there an equation you can point me to where I can calculate ground temperature myself (given a combination of air temperature and solar radiation)?

Best
Adam

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Ground Temperature
parts:
Hi Adam,

You can certainly manually input data to the microclimate model by creating your own script - see this example for instance - from the NicheMapR vignettes. But you need to be careful - it's easy to get wrong (e.g. with units).

Ground temperature in the model is calculated as part of an overall solution of the substrate heat budget that involves the movement of heat in and out of the substrate with lag factors that depend on the heat capacity of the substrate interacting with the fluctuating environment above ground, and is quite a complex thing to calculate (partial differential equations for change in heat through time and depth are being solved in the microclimate model). In the FORTRAN code the line where the rate of change of the surface is calculated is here. You could also use TrenchR's function 'soil_temperature' (see the associated vignette on microclimates).

All the best,
Mike
